correctness.rationale: Every nonzero order-preserving partial isometry has unique translation displacement, with powers corresponding exactly to consecutive occupied steps in residue chains. The binary forbidden-run polynomial follows from a unique word decomposition. Two displacement signs and a single empty map produce the stated bivariate cumulative count. A direct-composition exhaustive check through n=11 confirms every coefficient. For fixed d, factorial moments of minimally started k-runs converge to Poisson(theta/2); geometric tightness of displacement gives the same law in the nilpotent ensemble. The upper and lower tails imply bounded lattice fluctuations.

value.rationale: Least zero power is a natural nilpotent-depth invariant not determined by domain rank. The polynomial resolves all ranks and depths simultaneously in a standard inverse transformation monoid, and the lattice limit quantifies its typical depth. The result is more informative than a restatement of a known nilpotent total or a standalone binary-word identity.
